public.title: Spreadsheet III
public.description: input {cells,operations}; initial cells map names to integers or {sum:[names]} and are acyclic. Operations are get {cell}, set {cell,value} (must keep graph acyclic), or trySet {cell,value}. A trySet commits only if the entire resulting graph is acyclic, emitting true on success and false on rejection; rejection restores the prior value or absence. Get emits current recursively evaluated integer with missing cells as zero; set emits nothing. Return all emitted results. At most 12 cells, 20 operations, 3 terms/formula, accepted dependency depth 5. Supported inputs are valid for this contract. Aggregate JSON-serialized input is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes, nesting depth at most 6, arrays at most 40 items, operation/call lists at most 20 items, and individual strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless a tighter bound is stated. Integers have absolute value at most 1000; output arithmetic stays within safe integers. String object keys and string path segments are nonempty safe alphanumeric/underscore names excluding __proto__, constructor and prototype. Empty arrays/objects are allowed where consistent with the contract. Output ordering follows the rules above. These bounds include all nested payloads and all operations together.
hints: Separate the documented JSON representation from the behavior being modeled.
Preserve ordering and distinguish missing values, null, zero and false carefully.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, fixtures and reference solutions, 2026. Covers a common JavaScript practice topic; no third-party exercise text or implementation copied.

explanation: Tentatively write, detect cycles using active recursion paths, and roll back rejected writes. Naive full validation is O(V times 3 to the V) worst case on this bounded graph; accepted reads use depth at most 5. Space O(V) for recursion paths and stored cells. Functional tests check the documented adapter behavior; they do not enforce implementation technique or prohibit built-in APIs.
